request.spec:
Show the activity of the sheet: for every user and every event in the sheet's audit file, one
line <user> <EVENT> <count>, sorted by user then event.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show the activity of the sheet: for every user and every event in the sheet's audit file, one
line <user> <EVENT> <count>, sorted by user then event.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added a sheet activity view next to the Audit section. For every user and every event in the sheet's audit file it shows one line, `<user> <EVENT> <count>`, sorted by user then event. `bin/e2e` builds and runs the app, and all 4 tests pass: the activity test and the three existing scenarios.

- **Server:** `Audit.activity(sheetId)` counts the sheet's records by the user and the event at the start of each line. A new read-only endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/audit/activity`, returns those lines and writes nothing to the store or the audit file.
- **Front end:** the audit viewer (`audit-viewer.ts`) now has a "Show activity" button (`activity-show`) and a list of `activity-line` items. Each press clears the old list before the new one loads. If the request fails, an `activity-error` message shows. Loading a sheet clears the list.

Sorting is plain alphabetical and case-sensitive, so a capitalised name like "Bob" would come before "amy".

No database schema change was needed, since the counts are worked out from the audit file each time.
